idea: A coding-agent skill rebuilds a motion video as inline SVG and one GSAP timeline you can edit.

claims.text: motion2code is a skill for coding agents that rebuilds a motion design video as inline SVG shapes animated by one GSAP timeline.
The output seeks frame by frame, loops seamlessly, and is checked side by side against the source.
The Think Big example is 10 seconds and 24 KB.

scenes.heading: MOTION2CODE: A MOTION VIDEO, *AS CODE*
scenes.say: Motion designers keep animation in a video file, so every change means a re-render. This skill rebuilds the animation as code your coding agent can edit.

scenes.heading: ONE TIMELINE, *SEEKABLE*
scenes.say: The output is inline SVG shapes on one GSAP timeline. It seeks frame by frame, loops cleanly, and is checked side by side against the source.

scenes.label: for the 10-second Think Big example
scenes.say: The Think Big example is ten seconds and twenty-four kilobytes, all in code.

scenes.heading: THE *CATCH*
cons: You need a coding agent to run the skill
Frame checks are a quality gate, not a guarantee
pros: Works with Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and more
scenes.say: The catch: you need a coding agent to run it, and the frame check is a quality gate, not a promise. Cursor and others work too, and the repo is MIT.
Would you edit your motion as code? Tell me what you animate in the comments.
